A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same WaterSIC research. Their complete main texts, equations, figures, tables and appendices support comparison, including matching relocated material.

before.justification: v1 reports original WaterSIC perplexity, zero-shot accuracy, component ablations and compression measurements.

after.justification: v2 retains original empirical results and adds fine-tuning, cross-corpus, calibration-sensitivity and larger-model experiments.

M1.justification: Section 4 adds WaterSIC-FT, which freezes integer codes and trains continuous rescalers using teacher-student distillation. Rate assignment changes from binary search to a secant method, and Appendix D now matches the target rate at each adaptive-mixing candidate instead of reusing an initially selected scale.

E1.justification: v1 uses WikiText-2 for calibration and perplexity evaluation alongside downstream benchmarks. v2 adds C4 perplexity evaluation, RedPajama calibration, and C4/RedPajama fine-tuning, substantially expanding corpus coverage and testing transfer beyond the calibration distribution. Existing downstream tasks remain.

E2.justification: The original comparison sets are retained. New longer-context comparisons include reported results for AQLM, DB-LLM, PV-Tuning, YAQA-B and QuIP (Tables 10 and 13). The new Llama-3-70B comparison additionally includes PB-LLM and OstQuant (Table 14); these are actual comparison entries, not merely citations.

E3.justification: v2 supplements the retained 2048-token evaluations with 4096- and 8192-token protocols, compares 1024 versus 2048 calibration contexts, and evaluates Llama-3-70B. It introduces fine-tuning budgets and controlled corpus comparisons using matched sequence counts. Appendix D also changes the reported mixing-search budget from 15 to 10 iterations.

E4.justification: The original component ablations remain. v2 adds Gaussian-versus-Laplace weight-distribution diagnostics (Figure 11), calibration-context sensitivity (Table 12), and calibration/fine-tuning corpus analyses across rates (Tables 15–16 and Figure 15). These test theoretical applicability and distribution sensitivity absent from v1.

E5.justification: Appendix E introduces distribution-fitting statistics: Kolmogorov–Smirnov distances to fitted Gaussian and Laplace distributions, averaged across layers with closer-fit counts. This adds statistical estimation and reporting, but neither version reports repeated-run uncertainty, confidence intervals or formal significance tests.

E6.justification: Most original benchmark entries remain, while v2 adds extensive fine-tuned, C4, longer-context and 70B results. For example, Table 2 retains Qwen3-8B WaterSIC perplexity 11.37 at 2.125 bits and adds 10.18 for the separately trained WaterSIC-FT configuration. Figure 5 also changes its reported rate-distribution statistics.

T1.justification: v2 corrects the rate definition by adding 1/n, fixes the matrix-factor placement in Appendix B Equation (35), and restores the addition sign in Appendix C's regularized objective. The principal theorem, assumptions and proof strategy remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction retain the headline claims: unequal channel rates, the 0.255-bit information-theoretic gap, potentially unbounded GPTQ suboptimality, and state-of-the-art Llama/Qwen performance over 1–4 bits. The added experiments do not revise these central claims.

C2.justification: v2 adds substantive interpretations of Gaussian applicability and query/key deviations, calibration-distribution mismatch, corpus-dependent fine-tuning benefits, and calibration-context tradeoffs. Fine-tuning is removed from the future-work discussion, although statements restricting the work to layerwise optimization and small-to-mid-sized models remain outdated.

D1.justification: v2 adds an implementation link and detailed fine-tuning instructions: AdamW settings, learning-rate schedule, four epochs, checkpointing, CPU caching, streamed integer codes and rescaler precision handling. It also reports four H100 GPUs for Llama-3-70B and documents the revised rate-search procedure. The linked resource's availability cannot be verified from the PDFs alone.

R1.justification: v2 adds positioning through prediction-based Gaussian rate-distortion theory (Zamir et al., 2006), outlier-safe pretraining (Park et al., 2025), and a source for 70B comparisons (Huang et al., 2024). The prior-work review is largely retained; most other reference edits update publication metadata.

P1.justification: v2 expands the introductory explanation, revises procedural prose, adds acknowledgements, and separates supplementary model evaluations into Appendix F while moving zero-shot evaluations to Appendix G. Most existing exposition, theory and prior-work text remains substantially unchanged.

P2.justification: The model-size plot moves from v1 Figure 3 to v2 Figure 1 with a logarithmic size axis and additional curves. Main comparison plots become side-by-side displays; algorithms and appendix tables are relocated and compacted. New diagnostic figures and experimental tables substantially revise the presentation beyond renumbering or numerical updates.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially strengthens empirical assessability through cross-corpus controls, matched-context comparisons with stronger methods, and 70B evaluation, addressing gaps explicitly deferred in v1. Fine-tuning documentation and mathematical corrections also help. These gains outweigh reporting weaknesses, but reconciliation is needed: 1-bit Llama-3.2-1B fine-tuned perplexity is 30.47 in Table 1 versus 32.85 in Tables 7 and 16, and broad SOTA and scope statements are not fully aligned with the expanded evidence.
